items.title: Tenbrugge
items.content: A professional WordPress website for Ten Bruggen that presents financial and accountancy services in a clear, trustworthy and accessible way. The website combines strong structure, responsive design and direct contact options to help visitors quickly find the right expertise.
items.excerpt: For Ten Bruggen, I created a modern and responsive WordPress website focused on clarity, credibility and conversion. Complex financial services were translated into an easy-to-navigate structure with clear service pages, strong calls to action and integrated appointment booking. The result is a professional website that supports both the brand and the customer journey.

items.title: Recruiter Case Study - Static Prototype
items.content:
Selected case · WordPress / WooCommerce

Byderma — structuring treatments, booking and ecommerce in one WordPress platform

Byderma combines multiple beauty treatments, appointment booking, a large WooCommerce catalogue and member benefits. I structured the WordPress and WooCommerce experience so each journey stays clear while the platform still feels consistent across desktop and mobile.

Visit live Byderma site View all cases

Role

WordPress Developer

Platform

WordPress + WooCommerce

Focus

UX · Ecommerce · Responsive

Journeys

Treatments · Shop · Booking

01 · The challenge

Three core journeys, one coherent beauty platform

The business combines treatment discovery, appointment booking and ecommerce, with member content supporting those journeys. The challenge was to keep those needs from competing for attention while the experience still feels like one Byderma platform.

Treatment discovery

Multiple treatment categories need enough context to help visitors choose and then move naturally toward booking.

Booking handoff

Treatment information needs a clear route into appointment booking without turning every service page into a commerce flow.

Commerce & member support

The WooCommerce catalogue stays product-focused, while member and account content remains accessible without interrupting the primary journeys.

02 · My contribution

I translated that business complexity into a clear WordPress information architecture

My role was WordPress developer. I structured how treatments, booking, WooCommerce and supporting member content relate to each other, then carried the same hierarchy through to smaller screens.

01

Information architecture

I separated treatment discovery, shopping and booking into distinct paths so users can immediately understand what kind of task they are in.

02

WooCommerce journey

I kept product discovery and purchasing focused inside the shop, while treatment information hands off naturally to appointments.

03

Responsive hierarchy

I preserved the same task priority on mobile instead of collapsing different intents into one generic flow.

03 · Engineering decisions

WordPress decisions behind a mixed service-and-commerce platform

The value of this case is not just the finished interface; it is how the platform is organised. WordPress and WooCommerce support different user intents without forcing treatment discovery, booking and ecommerce into one generic flow.

Verified stack
WordPress · WooCommerce

Architecture
Treatment discovery · appointment routes · product discovery · member/account support

Responsive principle
Preserve the same hierarchy and task separation on smaller screens

Evidence
Live Byderma site · verified project media across desktop, tablet and mobile

04 · Live proof

The structure is visible in the live product and responsive project captures

Byderma.nl currently exposes the same core model: treatment categories, appointment booking, a product boutique and member benefits. The verified project media below shows the interface across desktop, tablet and mobile.

Desktop homepage Tablet layout Mobile layout Mobile conversion flow

Outcome
The live platform keeps treatment discovery, booking, ecommerce and member support recognisable as separate tasks inside one brand experience.

This case shows how I translate mixed service and ecommerce requirements into a clear WordPress and WooCommerce experience, with decisions that remain understandable across desktop and mobile.

What I bring to a WordPress team

WordPress & WooCommerce Development

Structured websites and webshops with reusable sections, clean editing flows and less unnecessary plugin dependency.

Elementor & ACF Builds

Editable page structures that clients can manage without breaking layout, content or design consistency.

Performance, WCAG & Technical SEO

Core Web Vitals, accessible structure, lighter assets and technical SEO improvements that support speed, usability and search visibility.

GitHub, QA & Automation

Git/GitHub, GitHub Actions and Playwright for safer changes, repeatable checks and reliable delivery.

Experience

10+ years of front-end, UX and WordPress experience

My background combines front-end development, UX thinking, SEO and WordPress. I use Git/GitHub, automated checks and structured QA to keep work reliable and maintainable after launch.

2016 — 2017

Bergo

Front-End Developer

Bergo was where I learned how a webshop works in practice. Working with developers and designers, I kept Magento pages clear, tidy and easy to use. That job gave me a solid start in building and improving websites.

2017 — 2018

Blueprint Sound Academy

Front-End Developer

Blueprint Sound Academy gave me more room to work on the look and feel of a website. Small changes to layouts, navigation and page details made the site feel more consistent. From there, I started paying more attention to how people move through a website.

2018 — 2019

Kamernet

UX Designer

At Kamernet, the user came first. Simple sketches and test screens helped us see where people got stuck before we built the final version. Their feedback showed me how a few small changes could make the whole journey easier.

2019 — 2020

Easytheorie

WordPress Developer

Easytheorie was where WordPress became part of my everyday work. Clearer pages, better content and work on Google search helped people find the right information faster. WordPress, design and content started to come together for me there.

2020 — 2021

Wube

WordPress Developer

Wube was where I started building complete WordPress websites for clients. Each project had different wishes, so I learned to turn them into a site that looked good and stayed easy to manage. Before launch, I checked phones, different browsers and speed so the site was ready to use.

2021 — Present

Webactueel

Senior WordPress Developer

Today at Webactueel, I work on WordPress and WooCommerce sites from start to finish. Some days I build pages, other days I fix a plugin, speed up a site or solve a client problem. Over time, I have made my own checks and tools so I can spot issues earlier and keep the work reliable.

Engineering workflow

How I work remotely: plan, build, automate, verify

I work async-friendly and evidence-first: changes are scoped, versioned, reviewable, tested and verified before handoff.

Plan and scope

Define the goal, user journey, content model and technical boundaries before implementation.

Build in WordPress

Build with WordPress, WooCommerce, Elementor, ACF and custom PHP/JavaScript while keeping editing maintainable.

Version and automate

Use Git/GitHub, reviewable commits, GitHub Actions/CI and repeatable checks instead of manual-only delivery.

Test and ship

Use Playwright, Core Web Vitals and WCAG checks, then verify deployment and readback before completion.

Remote WordPress roles

Hiring a senior WordPress developer for a remote team?

Best fit: senior WordPress/front-end roles where I can own builds, debugging, WooCommerce, Elementor/ACF, performance and release quality. Based in Rotterdam (CET), open to remote roles across NL/EU — permanent or contract.
